decision: Add a Keycloak 25.x service to docker-compose.yml (additive, postgres block untouched) using start-dev mode with import-on-start realm provisioning; Keycloak internal store = existing Postgres instance on dedicated 'keycloak' schema (single-substrate principle); host port 8180; realm JSON committed at config/keycloak/realm-choros.json with 7 human dev accounts (matching org.ts fixture), one choros-api confidential client, one actor_type protocol mapper (oidc-usermodel-attribute-mapper → claim actor_type), and representative agent-orchestrator service-account client; CHOROS_AUTH_MODE env var (default: dev) is the migration seam — dev mode keeps x-dev-user stub intact (all existing tests unchanged), keycloak mode is a stub T-0060 fills; JWT contract frozen: iss=realm-URL, aud includes choros-api, actor_type claim human|agent, RS256.

rejected_alternatives.option: Embedded H2 for Keycloak internal store
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates single-Postgres-per-silo principle (stack ADR). H2 is container-ephemeral without an explicit volume; state is lossy on restart. A dedicated 'keycloak' schema on the existing Postgres instance is consistent, operationally simpler (one backup), and aligned with the silo substrate model established by T-0053.

25.x is the latest stable OSS at design time. No feature gap between 24 and 25 for this task. The coder may downgrade to 24.x without escalation if a 25.x issue is found — the ACs are version-agnostic per spec §7.

8080 is a common developer-machine default used by many tools; Keycloak itself defaults to 8080 in start-dev, so an ambient Keycloak would collide. 8180 (8080+100 offset) is the conventional secondary HTTP port used in Keycloak's own multi-instance docs.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keycloak Operator / Helm / external provisioning tool
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Overkill for a dev/silo compose stack; adds a non-trivial dependency and a new language surface. Keycloak's built-in --import-realm is battle-tested and zero-dep for this use case.

rejected_alternatives.option: Bootstrap script using Admin REST API calls at start time
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Fragile: depends on timing (Keycloak must be fully ready), adds a shell/curl dependency, and provisioning state is not committed to git (no audit trail). JSON realm import is declarative, committed, and applied atomically on first start.

rejected_alternatives.option: Shared realm (pooled tenancy) instead of dedicated realm
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Explicitly rejected by tenancy-and-delivery.md §6 and spec §0. Keycloak Organizations (shared realm for pooled SaaS) is deferred with pooled mode. One realm = one silo contour is ratified.

rejected_alternatives.option: Remove x-dev-user path (require JWT from day 1)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Breaks AC-9: all existing e2e tests (auth.e2e.test.ts, inbox.e2e.test.ts) use x-dev-user and would require a live Keycloak. The spec mandates the migration seam: dev-auth stays intact under CHOROS_AUTH_MODE=dev.

rejected_alternatives.option: Scatter CHOROS_AUTH_MODE check across every route handler
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Creates untestable scattered guard logic. The correct model is one env-var read at the auth-middleware layer in src/http/auth.ts — one branch point, not N. T-0060 fills the keycloak branch in the same single location.

object_model.entity: HumanUser (one per org.ts human employee — 7 total)

fields.name: dev branch
fields.type: behaviour — x-dev-user stub active; identical to today

fields.name: keycloak branch
fields.type: behaviour — x-dev-user disabled; Bearer JWT expected (T-0060 implements)

contracts: JWT contract (frozen for T-0060): iss = http://<host>:<port>/realms/<realm>; aud MUST include 'choros-api'; sub = non-empty UUID string; preferred_username = employee-id (human) or client_id (agent); actor_type = 'human' | 'agent' (via actor-type-mapper on choros-api client); alg = RS256 (or ES256 if configured).

CHOROS_AUTH_MODE seam: env var read in src/http/auth.ts; default 'dev'; 'dev' = x-dev-user stub active (existing behaviour, no change); 'keycloak' = x-dev-user disabled, Bearer JWT expected (T-0060 fills this branch). T-0060 reads the same var.
Realm JSON path contract: config/keycloak/realm-choros.json — committed, valid JSON, not gitignored, authoritative realm definition. Keycloak mounts it via /opt/keycloak/data/import/:ro on start-dev.

Compose additive contract: docker-compose.yml gains a 'keycloak' service block; the 'postgres' service block is unmodified. The postgres+keycloak stack comes up with 'docker compose up -d'. 'depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy' ensures ordering.
Port contract: KEYCLOAK_PORT default = 8180. Not 5432, 55432, or 3000. Documented in docs/environments.md.

Keycloak internal store contract: KC_DB=postgres; KC_DB_URL points to the same Postgres instance (postgres service, port 5432 internal) with currentSchema=keycloak; Keycloak bootstraps 'keycloak' schema itself. choros_migrator role is used for dev; choros_app is NOT granted access to the keycloak schema.

Human fixture contract: all 7 type='human' persons from src/http/org.ts ORG_SEED are present as Keycloak users: e-kravtsova, e-mironov, e-larina, e-orlov, e-savina, e-petrov, e-belov. Each has actor_type=human attribute and credentials[password]=dev-pw-<username>.

Agent client contract: at least one client with serviceAccountsEnabled=true, clientId matching 'agent-*' prefix, directAccessGrantsEnabled=false, and service-account user attribute actor_type=agent. Representative client: agent-orchestrator.
docs/environments.md update contract: file MUST contain KEYCLOAK_PORT, KEYCLOAK_REALM, CHOROS_AUTH_MODE, core API client-id (choros-api), and a note on adding users/agents.

Public-surface compat contract (FE-W23-0008): DEV_USER_HEADER export from src/http/auth.ts unchanged; createServer, handleRequest, registerAuthRoutes, findEmployee, listSelectableUsers signatures unchanged. CHOROS_AUTH_MODE is an internal constant, not exported.

fitness_functions.rule: Keycloak health endpoint GET /health/ready returns HTTP 200 within 120 s of docker compose up -d keycloak
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-kc: ci/checks/kc/wait-ready.sh — polls GET http://localhost:${KEYCLOAK_PORT:-8180}/health/ready every 5 s for up to 120 s (24 retries); non-200 after timeout = fail

fitness_functions.rule: Realm provisioned on first start (import-on-start, no manual admin-UI); OIDC discovery URL returns 200 with issuer matching http://localhost:8180/realms/choros
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-kc: ci/checks/kc/realm-ready.sh — curl GET /realms/choros/.well-known/openid-configuration after FF-1 passes; assert HTTP 200 and jq '.issuer' matches pattern http://localhost:8180/realms/choros

fitness_functions.rule: Human user obtains access token via ROPC grant (e-kravtsova, dev password) against choros-api client — HTTP 200, non-empty access_token
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-kc: ci/checks/kc/human-token.sh — POST /realms/choros/protocol/openid-connect/token with grant_type=password, client_id=choros-api, client_secret, username=e-kravtsova, password=dev-pw-kravtsova; assert HTTP 200 and jq '.access_token | length > 0'

fitness_functions.rule: Agent service account obtains access token via client_credentials grant (agent-orchestrator) — HTTP 200, non-empty access_token
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-kc: ci/checks/kc/agent-token.sh — POST /realms/choros/protocol/openid-connect/token with grant_type=client_credentials, client_id=agent-orchestrator, client_secret=agent-orchestrator-dev-secret; assert HTTP 200 and jq '.access_token | length > 0'

fitness_functions.rule: JWT claims contract: decoded access tokens from FF-3 (human) and FF-4 (agent) each contain iss matching realm URL pattern, aud containing choros-api, non-empty sub, non-empty preferred_username, actor_type='human' for human and 'agent' for agent, JWT header alg=RS256
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-kc: ci/checks/kc/jwt-claims.sh — base64-decode JWT payload+header from FF-3/FF-4 tokens; jq assertions: .iss matches '^http://localhost:8180/realms/choros$'; (.aud | if type=="array" then contains(["choros-api"]) else .=="choros-api" end); .sub | length > 0; .preferred_username | length > 0; human token .actor_type=="human"; agent token .actor_type=="agent"; header .alg=="RS256"

fitness_functions.rule: Realm JSON committed at config/keycloak/realm-choros.json, is valid JSON, and is not gitignored
fitness_functions.ci_check: static-now: ci/checks/kc/realm-json-exists.sh — test -f config/keycloak/realm-choros.json (file exists); python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('config/keycloak/realm-choros.json'))" (valid JSON); git check-ignore -q config/keycloak/realm-choros.json && exit 1 || true (not gitignored)

fitness_functions.rule: All 7 human users from org.ts fixture present in realm JSON: e-kravtsova, e-mironov, e-larina, e-orlov, e-savina, e-petrov, e-belov
fitness_functions.ci_check: static-now: ci/checks/kc/fixture-users.sh — for each of the 7 usernames: jq --arg u <name> '[.users[].username] | contains([$u])' config/keycloak/realm-choros.json must return true; all 7 must pass

fitness_functions.rule: At least one client with serviceAccountsEnabled=true and clientId matching 'agent-*' pattern in realm JSON
fitness_functions.ci_check: static-now: ci/checks/kc/agent-client.sh — jq '[.clients[] | select(.serviceAccountsEnabled==true and (.clientId | startswith("agent-")))] | length' config/keycloak/realm-choros.json returns integer >= 1

fitness_functions.rule: Full test suite passes with CHOROS_AUTH_MODE=dev (or unset); zero failures in auth.e2e.test.ts and inbox.e2e.test.ts; x-dev-user path is active
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-dev: existing CI job (npm run ci) with CHOROS_AUTH_MODE=dev or default; all tests pass; no regression from T-0054 changes

fitness_functions.rule: CHOROS_AUTH_MODE env var is read in src/http/auth.ts (or src/server.ts); default is 'dev'; var name and values documented in docs/environments.md
fitness_functions.ci_check: static-now: grep -r 'CHOROS_AUTH_MODE' src/ returns at least one match in src/http/auth.ts or src/server.ts; grep confirms default fallback to 'dev' in the same file; FF-14 covers docs/environments.md documentation

fitness_functions.rule: No prod credential committed; dev credentials in realm JSON labeled DEV ONLY; compose vars use ${VAR:-default} form; no credential literal in TS source
fitness_functions.ci_check: static-now: ci/checks/kc/no-prod-secret.sh — (a) git grep -i 'choros_kc_dev_pw|choros_dev_pw|dev-pw-|dev-secret' src/ returns 0 matches; (b) grep -i 'DEV ONLY\|dev-only' config/keycloak/realm-choros.json returns >= 1 match; (c) grep 'KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD' docker-compose.yml confirms ${VAR:-default} form, not a literal password

fitness_functions.rule: docker compose up -d starts both postgres and keycloak; both healthchecks reach 'healthy' state
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-kc: docker compose up -d exits 0; docker compose ps shows postgres and keycloak both in status 'healthy' (or 'running' with passing healthcheck)

fitness_functions.rule: KEYCLOAK_PORT default in docker-compose.yml is 8180 (not 5432, 55432, or 3000)
fitness_functions.ci_check: static-now: grep 'KEYCLOAK_PORT' docker-compose.yml confirms default 8180 (pattern ${KEYCLOAK_PORT:-8180}); grep -E ':-5432|:-55432|:-3000' docker-compose.yml | grep -i keycloak returns 0 matches
